records.source: וַיַּ֥עַן אֱלִיה֗וּא וַיֹּאמַֽר׃
records.gloss: And answered Elihu and said:
pieces: Then Elihu answered:

decisions.choice: answered: took up speaking again
decisions.reason: No one has replied to Elihu's first speech (chapters 32-33), so "answered" here simply marks the start of a new speech, as it often does in Job. This is Elihu's second speech; Elihu son of Barachel the Buzite was introduced at 32:2. The introduction stays prose.

decisions.choice: Elihu: the young speaker who joins the debate after the three friends
decisions.reason: Elihu waited while the older men spoke (32:4-6). In this speech he turns from Job to the listening wise men and defends God's justice against what Job has said.

decisions.choice: said
decisions.reason: Readable uses the book-wide pattern for speech introductions: "Then Elihu said:".

records.heading: Elihu calls the wise to judge Job's words

records.source: שִׁמְע֣וּ חֲכָמִ֣ים מִלָּ֑י וְ֝יֹדְעִ֗ים הַאֲזִ֥ינוּ לִֽי׃
records.gloss: Hear, wise [ones], my words, and [you] knowing, give ear to me.
pieces: Hear my words, you who are wise; \q listen to me, you who have knowledge.

L.2: Hear my words, you wise ones; \q and you who know, give ear to me.

R.2: Listen to what I say, you wise people. \q You who know so much, hear me out.

decisions.choice: wise, knowing: the circle of wise listeners
decisions.reason: The verbs are plural, so Elihu addresses a group, not Job alone. They may be the three friends, or a wider circle of wise listeners whose verdict Elihu appeals to (verses 10 and 34). He may also be speaking a little ironically, since he has said that age alone does not make people wise (32:9).

decisions.choice: hear ... give ear: two calls to listen in parallel
decisions.reason: The two lines say the same thing twice, as Hebrew poetry does; "give ear" is the poetic partner of "hear" (Psalm 49:2).

decisions.choice: wise ones / you who are wise
decisions.reason: The Hebrew plural adjective names no sex, and wise listeners could be men or women, so English avoids supplying "men".

records.source: כִּי־אֹ֭זֶן מִלִּ֣ין תִּבְחָ֑ן וְ֝חֵ֗ךְ יִטְעַ֥ם לֶאֱכֹֽל׃
records.gloss: For [the] ear words tests, and [the] palate tastes to eat.
pieces: For the ear tests words \q as the tongue tastes food.

L.3: For the ear tests words \q as the palate tastes food.

R.3: Your ears can tell good words from bad, \q just as your mouth can tell good food from bad.

decisions.choice: Elihu quotes Job's own saying
decisions.reason: Job said almost exactly this in 12:11. Elihu turns Job's words back on him: let the listeners test Job's claims the way the tongue tests food.

decisions.choice: tests, tastes: judges what is good
decisions.reason: Hearing is pictured as tasting: a careful listener sorts true words from false the way the mouth sorts good food from bad. Verse 4 draws the conclusion.

decisions.choice: as
decisions.reason: The Hebrew joins the two lines with "and", but the second line is a comparison for the first; English shows that with "as".

decisions.choice: tongue
decisions.reason: "Palate" is the exact word; Balanced uses the more everyday "tongue" for the organ of taste.

records.source: מִשְׁפָּ֥ט נִבְחֲרָה־לָּ֑נוּ נֵדְעָ֖ה בֵינֵ֣ינוּ מַה־טּֽוֹב׃
records.gloss: Justice let us choose for ourselves; let us know among ourselves what [is] good.
pieces: Let us choose for ourselves what is right; \q let us decide together what is good.

L.4: Let us choose for ourselves what is just; \q let us know among ourselves what [is] good.

R.4: Let us decide together what is right \q and agree on what is good.

decisions.choice: justice: the right verdict in Job's case
decisions.reason: The word (mishpat) means justice, a right ruling. It is the key word of this chapter: Job says God took away his right (verse 5), and Elihu insists God never perverts justice (verse 12).

decisions.choice: choose, know: test and settle on
decisions.reason: To choose here is to examine and decide, as a judge chooses between claims; "let us know" means let us come to agree. Elihu invites the listeners to act as a court.

decisions.choice: what is just / what is right
decisions.reason: English needs a phrase to say that the listeners are to choose a just verdict, not an abstract quality.

records.source: כִּֽי־אָ֭מַר אִיּ֣וֹב צָדַ֑קְתִּי וְ֝אֵ֗ל הֵסִ֥יר מִשְׁפָּטִֽי׃
records.gloss: For has said Job, I am righteous, and God has taken away my right.
pieces: For Job has said, "I am in the right, \q but God has denied me justice.

L.5: For Job has said, "I am righteous, \q and God has taken away my right.

R.5: Job has said, "I am innocent, \q but God refuses to treat me fairly.

decisions.choice: Elihu sums up Job's words
decisions.reason: Elihu quotes Job freely: "I am righteous" sums up 13:18 and 27:6, and "God has taken away my right" is almost word for word 27:2. The quotation runs on into verse 6.

decisions.choice: I am righteous: I am in the right, innocent in this case
decisions.reason: The verb (tsadaq) is used as in a court: Job claims to be in the right in his dispute with God, not to be sinless.

decisions.choice: my right: the justice due to me
decisions.reason: The same word as "justice" in verse 4 (mishpat), here the ruling Job is owed.

decisions.choice: but
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "and" joins two clauses that stand against each other; Balanced and Readable show the contrast.

records.source: עַל־מִשְׁפָּטִ֥י אֲכַזֵּ֑ב אָנ֖וּשׁ חִצִּ֣י בְלִי־פָֽשַׁע׃
records.gloss: Concerning my right I lie; incurable [is] my arrow without transgression.
pieces: Though I am in the right, I am called a liar; \q my wound from the arrow cannot be healed, though I have not rebelled."

L.6: Despite my right, I am [counted] a liar; \q my arrow [wound is] incurable, without transgression."

R.6: I am right, but I am treated as a liar. \q God's arrow has wounded me past healing, though I have done nothing wrong."

decisions.choice: Despite my right, I am counted a liar
alternatives: Should I lie about my right?
decisions.reason: The words are "concerning my right I lie". Read as a statement, Job complains that though he is in the right he is treated as a liar. Read as a question, he refuses to lie by confessing a guilt he does not have (27:5-6). Both fit Job's words; the statement fits the second line better.

decisions.choice: my arrow: the arrow that wounds me
decisions.reason: Job has said that the arrows of the Almighty are in him (6:4; compare 16:13). "My arrow" means the wound God's arrow has made.

decisions.choice: without transgression: though I have not rebelled
decisions.reason: The word (pesha) is rebellion against God. Job insists his suffering has no such cause.

decisions.choice: God's arrow
decisions.reason: Readable names the one Job says shot the arrow (6:4).

records.source: מִי־גֶ֥בֶר כְּאִיּ֑וֹב יִֽשְׁתֶּה־לַּ֥עַג כַּמָּֽיִם׃
records.gloss: Who [is] a man like Job? He drinks scorn like water.
pieces: Who is there like Job, \q who drinks up scorn like water?

L.7: What man [is] like Job, \q [who] drinks scorn like water?

R.7: Is there anyone else like Job? \q He soaks up mocking talk as easily as he drinks water.

decisions.choice: drinks scorn like water: takes in mockery freely and greedily
decisions.reason: Eliphaz said that mortals drink injustice like water (15:16). Here Job is said to drink in scorn, that is, to indulge freely in mocking talk against God; verse 8 says he keeps company with the wicked. Some take it instead that Job swallows the scorn others heap on him, but the following verses are an accusation.

decisions.choice: a man: Job himself
decisions.reason: The word (gever) is used of Job, a particular man, so no inclusive wording is needed.

records.source: וְאָרַ֣ח לְ֭חֶבְרָה עִם־פֹּ֣עֲלֵי אָ֑וֶן וְ֝לָלֶ֗כֶת עִם־אַנְשֵׁי־רֶֽשַׁע׃
records.gloss: And he travels for company with doers of evil and to walk with men of wickedness.
pieces: He keeps company with evildoers \q and goes about with the wicked.

L.8: And he travels in company with doers of evil, \q and walks with {{gender:people|men}} of wickedness.

R.8: He goes around with people who do evil \q and spends his time with the wicked.

decisions.choice: travels, walks with the wicked: shares their way
decisions.reason: To walk with someone is to share their way of life (Psalm 1:1; Proverbs 13:20). Elihu does not say Job has done what the wicked do; verse 9 shows he means Job talks as they talk.

decisions.choice: doers of evil: those who practice wickedness
decisions.reason: A common phrase in Job and the Psalms (31:3; 34:22; Psalm 5:6).

decisions.choice: {{gender:people|men}} of wickedness
decisions.reason: The phrase means wicked people in general, so the gender setting offers the inclusive form.

records.source: כִּֽי־אָ֭מַר לֹ֣א יִסְכָּן־גָּ֑בֶר בִּ֝רְצֹת֗וֹ עִם־אֱלֹהִֽים׃
records.gloss: For he has said, Not it profits a man in his delighting with God.
pieces: For he has said, "It does no one any good \q to be on good terms with God."

L.9: For he has said, "It does not profit {{gender:a person|a man}} \q when {{gender:they take|he takes}} delight in God."

R.9: He has said, "It does not help anyone \q to try to please God."

decisions.choice: Elihu's summary of Job's position
decisions.reason: Job never says this in these words. Elihu draws it from 9:22 ("he destroys both the blameless and the wicked") and from Job's picture of the wicked who ask what profit there is in prayer (21:15). Elihu returns to it in 35:3.

decisions.choice: delighting with God: being in God's favor, pleasing God
decisions.reason: The verb (ratsah) means to be pleased with, or to be accepted by. Here it is a life of friendship with God and pleasing him.

decisions.choice: {{gender:a person|a man}} ... {{gender:they take|he takes}}
decisions.reason: The word (gever) here means anyone; Literal keeps the singular with a gender setting.

decisions.choice: no one / anyone
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "anyone", which is already inclusive.

records.source: לָכֵ֤ן׀אַ֥נֲשֵׁ֥ילֵבָ֗ב שִׁמְע֫וּ לִ֥י חָלִ֖לָה לָאֵ֥ל מֵרֶ֗שַׁע וְשַׁדַּ֥י מֵעָֽוֶל׃
records.gloss: Therefore, men of heart, listen to me: far be it to God from wickedness, and [the] Almighty from wrong.
pieces: So listen to me, you {{gender:people|men}} of understanding: \q God would never do evil, \q the Almighty would never do wrong.

L.10: Therefore, {{gender:people|men}} of heart, listen to me: \q far be it from God [to do] wickedness, \q and [from] the Almighty [to do] wrong.

R.10: So listen to me, you who understand. \q God would never do evil. \q God All-Powerful would never do wrong.

decisions.choice: men of heart: people of understanding
decisions.reason: In Hebrew the heart is where a person thinks and understands, so "men of heart" are sensible people. Elihu again appeals to the wise listeners (verse 2).

decisions.choice: far be it: it is unthinkable
decisions.reason: The word (chalilah) is a strong denial, "it would be a profane thing" (Genesis 18:25, where Abraham says the same of the Judge of all the earth).

decisions.choice: the Almighty: Shaddai
decisions.reason: See the note at 5:17.

decisions.choice: {{gender:people|men}} of understanding
decisions.reason: The phrase names the listeners by their understanding, not their sex; the gender setting gives the traditional form.

decisions.choice: God All-Powerful
decisions.reason: Readable's form for Shaddai throughout the book.

records.source: כִּ֤י פֹ֣עַל אָ֭דָם יְשַׁלֶּם־ל֑וֹ וּֽכְאֹ֥רַח אִ֝֗ישׁ יַמְצִאֶֽנּוּ׃
records.gloss: For [the] work of a man he repays to him, and according to [the] way of a man he makes him find [it].
pieces: For {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} pays people back for what they do; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} brings on each one what their conduct deserves.

L.11: For {{gender:a person's|a man's}} work {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} repays to {{gender:them|him}}, \q and according to {{gender:their|his}} way {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} makes {{gender:them|him}} find [it].

R.11: God pays people back for what they have done. \q He gives each person what their way of life deserves.

decisions.choice: God repays each person according to their deeds
decisions.reason: This is the principle of retribution Elihu defends throughout (Psalm 62:13; Proverbs 24:12). Job does not deny it in general; he denies that it explains his own suffering.

decisions.choice: a man: any human being
decisions.reason: Both words (adam, ish) here mean any person, men and women alike.

decisions.choice: people, each one / each person
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the plural and "each", which are inclusive with no setting needed; Literal keeps the singular with gender settings.

decisions.choice: God
decisions.reason: Readable names the subject, which the Hebrew leaves to the context (verse 10).

records.source: אַף־אָמְנָ֗ם אֵ֥ל לֹֽא־יַרְשִׁ֑יעַ וְ֝שַׁדַּ֗י לֹֽא־יְעַוֵּ֥ת מִשְׁפָּֽט׃
records.gloss: Indeed, truly God not acts wickedly, and [the] Almighty not perverts justice.
pieces: Truly, God will never do wrong; \q the Almighty will never twist justice.

L.12: Yes, truly God does not act wickedly, \q and the Almighty does not pervert justice.

R.12: It is certain that God never does evil. \q God All-Powerful never makes justice crooked.

decisions.choice: pervert justice: echoes Bildad
decisions.reason: Bildad asked, "Does God pervert justice?" (8:3), with the same verb (ivvet). Elihu answers that question as firmly as Bildad did.

decisions.choice: indeed, truly: strong assertion
decisions.reason: Two emphatic words stand together; Elihu means there can be no doubt.

decisions.choice: God All-Powerful
decisions.reason: Readable's form for Shaddai.

records.source: מִֽי־פָקַ֣ד עָלָ֣יו אָ֑רְצָה וּמִ֥י שָׂ֝֗ם תֵּבֵ֥ל כֻּלָּֽהּ׃
records.gloss: Who appointed over him [the] earth? And who set [the] world, all of it?
pieces: Who gave {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} charge over the earth? \q Who put {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} over the whole world?

L.13: Who put the earth in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} charge? \q And who laid [on {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}] the whole world?

R.13: Did anyone put God in charge of the earth? \q Did someone give {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} the whole world to rule?

decisions.choice: No one gave God his authority
decisions.reason: The questions expect the answer "no one". God's rule is his own, not a post given him by someone above him, so he has no master to fear and no reason to rule unjustly. Verses 14-15 show what his power over all life means.

decisions.choice: set the whole world: put it in his care
decisions.reason: The verb (sim) is "put" or "set". With the first line, it most likely means "who put the whole world in his charge?"; it can also mean "who set the world in place?", which makes the same point.

decisions.choice: laid [on {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}]
decisions.reason: Literal supplies the object the parallel line implies.

decisions.choice: God
decisions.reason: Readable names God, whom the Hebrew calls only "him".

records.source: אִם־יָשִׂ֣ים אֵלָ֣יו לִבּ֑וֹ רוּח֥וֹ וְ֝נִשְׁמָת֗וֹ אֵלָ֥יו יֶאֱסֹֽף׃
records.gloss: If he sets to him his heart, his spirit and his breath to himself he gathers,
pieces: If {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} were to set {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mind on {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} alone \q and gather back to {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} spirit and breath,

L.14: If {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} should set {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} heart on {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} \q [and] gather to {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} spirit and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} breath,

R.14: If God thought only of {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} \q and took back {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} spirit and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} breath,

decisions.choice: set his heart on himself: think only of himself
alternatives: set his heart against a person
decisions.reason: The words are "if he sets his heart to him". Most likely "him" is God himself: if God cared only for himself and withdrew what he gives. Others take "him" to be a human being: if God turned his attention against a person. Some manuscripts and ancient versions read "if he turns back his heart".

decisions.choice: his spirit and his breath: the life-breath God gives
decisions.reason: The word (ruach) can be wind, breath or spirit; with "breath" (neshamah) it is the breath of life God breathes into living things (Genesis 2:7; Job 33:4; Psalm 104:29-30). If God gathered it back, all life would end (verse 15).

decisions.choice: spirit
decisions.reason: "Spirit" keeps the two different Hebrew words distinct in English; the pair together means the breath of life (m2).

decisions.choice: God
decisions.reason: Readable names God at the start of the new thought.

records.source: יִגְוַ֣ע כָּל־בָּשָׂ֣ר יָ֑חַד וְ֝אָדָ֗ם עַל־עָפָ֥ר יָשֽׁוּב׃
records.gloss: would expire all flesh together, and humankind to dust would return.
pieces: every living thing would die at once, \q and human beings would return to dust.

L.15: all flesh would expire together, \q and humankind would return to dust.

R.15: every living creature would die together, \q and people would turn back into dust.

decisions.choice: return to dust: as at the creation and the fall
decisions.reason: The words recall Genesis 3:19 ("to dust you will return"), and Psalm 104:29 and Ecclesiastes 12:7 say the same of God taking back the breath of life.

decisions.choice: all flesh: every living creature
decisions.reason: "All flesh" can mean all humankind or all living creatures (Genesis 6:17). With "humankind" in the next line it may be humankind, but the picture of God withdrawing breath covers every living thing (Psalm 104:29).

decisions.choice: every living thing / every living creature
decisions.reason: "All flesh" is not natural English for living beings; Balanced and Readable say what it means.

records.source: וְאִם־בִּ֥ינָה שִׁמְעָה־זֹּ֑את הַ֝אֲזִ֗ינָה לְק֣וֹל מִלָּֽי׃
records.gloss: And if understanding, hear this; give ear to [the] sound of my words.
pieces: If you have understanding, hear this; \q listen to what I am saying.

L.16: And if [you have] understanding, hear this; \q listen to the sound of my words.

R.16: If you are wise, listen to this. \q Pay attention to what I say.

decisions.choice: hear, listen: singular, now addressed to one person
decisions.reason: Elihu called the wise men in the plural (verses 2, 10). Here the commands are singular, so he turns to one listener, most likely Job, whom he addresses directly in verses 17 and 33.

decisions.choice: if understanding: if you have understanding
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has no verb; "if [there is] understanding" means "if you have any sense".

decisions.choice: [you have]
decisions.reason: Literal supplies the verb English needs.

records.source: הַאַ֬ף שׂוֹנֵ֣א מִשְׁפָּ֣ט יַחֲב֑וֹשׁ וְאִם־צַדִּ֖יק כַּבִּ֣יר תַּרְשִֽׁיעַ׃
records.gloss: Can even one hating justice govern? Or [the] righteous, mighty one will you condemn?
pieces: Can one who hates justice rule? \q Will you condemn the one who is righteous and mighty?

L.17: Can even one who hates justice govern? \q Or will you condemn the righteous, mighty one?

R.17: Could someone who hates justice rule the world? \q Will you call God guilty, when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is both righteous and mighty?

decisions.choice: govern: rule, hold in order
decisions.reason: The verb (chavash) means to bind; here it is to bind together under one's rule, to govern. A ruler who hated justice could not hold the world together.

decisions.choice: the righteous, mighty one: God
decisions.reason: The two words describe God: he is both just and all-powerful. Elihu asks Job whether he will declare guilty the very one who rules the world.

decisions.choice: condemn: declare guilty
decisions.reason: The verb (hirshia) is a court word, the opposite of "declare righteous" (Deuteronomy 25:1).

decisions.choice: call God guilty, when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is both righteous and mighty
decisions.reason: Readable names God and turns the two descriptions into a clause, so the question is clear.

records.source: הַאֲמֹ֣ר לְמֶ֣לֶךְ בְּלִיָּ֑עַל רָ֝שָׁ֗ע אֶל־נְדִיבִֽים׃
records.gloss: To say to a king, Worthless! Wicked! to nobles?
pieces: Would anyone say to a king, "You worthless man!" \q or to nobles, "You wicked men!"?

L.18: [Is it right] to say to a king, "Worthless!" \q [or] to nobles, "Wicked!"?

R.18: No one would dare to call a king worthless \q or tell nobles that they are wicked.

decisions.choice: Is it right to say: the infinitive, as the Hebrew is pointed
decisions.reason: As the Masoretic text is pointed, the word is an infinitive, "to say": no one may speak so to a king, still less to God. The Greek and other ancient versions read a participle, "who says": God is the one who calls kings worthless, which runs on into verse 19. The consonants allow both.

decisions.choice: worthless: belial, a good-for-nothing
decisions.reason: The word (beliyya'al) means worthless or base, a scoundrel (1 Samuel 25:25). It is a strong insult.

decisions.choice: You worthless man! ... You wicked men!
decisions.reason: Balanced shapes the bare words as the insults they are.

records.source: אֲשֶׁ֤ר לֹֽא־נָשָׂ֨א׀פְּנֵ֥י שָׂרִ֗ים וְלֹ֣א נִכַּר־שׁ֭וֹעַלִפְנֵי־דָ֑ל כִּֽי־מַעֲשֵׂ֖ה יָדָ֣יו כֻּלָּֽם׃
records.gloss: Who not lifts [the] faces of princes, and not regards [the] noble before [the] poor, for [the] work of his hands [are] all of them.
pieces: How much less to one who shows no favor to princes \q and does not regard the rich above the poor, \q for they are all the work of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hands!

L.19: [How much less to him] who does not lift up the faces of princes \q and does not regard the rich before the poor, \q for all of them [are the] work of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hands.

R.19: So how could anyone say that to God? \q He does not favor rulers or treat the rich better than the poor, \q because {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} made them all.

decisions.choice: lift up the faces: show favor, be partial
decisions.reason: To lift someone's face is to accept them, show them favor; in judgment it means partiality (Leviticus 19:15; Deuteronomy 10:17). God judges princes and the poor alike.

decisions.choice: all are the work of his hands
decisions.reason: God made rich and poor alike (Proverbs 22:2), so he has no reason to favor one over the other. Job said the same of himself and his servants (31:15).

decisions.choice: who: God, the one spoken of in verse 17
decisions.reason: The sentence goes back to the righteous, mighty one of verse 17. If one may not insult a king (verse 18), much less the one who rules kings.

decisions.choice: How much less to one who
decisions.reason: English needs the step from verse 18 to God spelled out; Literal brackets it.

decisions.choice: So how could anyone say that to God?
decisions.reason: Readable makes the comparison with verse 18 its own sentence.

records.source: רֶ֤גַע׀יָמֻתוּ֮ וַחֲצ֪וֹת לָ֥יְלָה יְגֹעֲשׁ֣וּ עָ֣ם וְיַעֲבֹ֑רוּ וְיָסִ֥ירוּ אַ֝בִּ֗יר לֹ֣א בְיָֽד׃
records.gloss: [In] a moment they die, and [at the] middle of [the] night are shaken a people and pass away, and they remove [the] mighty, not by hand.
pieces: In an instant they die; at midnight people are shaken and pass away; \q the mighty are removed, and no human hand does it.

L.20: In a moment they die; at midnight a people is shaken and passes away; \q and the mighty are taken away, not by [a human] hand.

R.20: They die in a moment, even in the middle of the night. \q Whole peoples are shaken and gone. \q Mighty rulers are taken away, but not by any human power.

decisions.choice: they die: rulers and peoples alike
decisions.reason: "They" are the princes and the rich of verse 19. Their power does not protect them; whole peoples fall with them.

decisions.choice: not by hand: by God's act, not by human means
decisions.reason: "Not by hand" means without human agency (Daniel 2:34; 8:25; Lamentations 4:6). God himself removes the mighty.

decisions.choice: middle of the night: suddenly, without warning
decisions.reason: Midnight is the hour of sudden judgment (Exodus 12:29).

decisions.choice: no human hand / any human power
decisions.reason: English "not by hand" would suggest something mechanical; Balanced and Readable say whose hand is meant (m2).

records.source: כִּי־עֵ֭ינָיו עַל־דַּרְכֵי־אִ֑ישׁ וְֽכָל־צְעָדָ֥יו יִרְאֶֽה׃
records.gloss: For his eyes [are] on [the] ways of a man, and all his steps he sees.
pieces: For {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} eyes are on the ways of everyone; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} sees every step they take.

L.21: For {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} eyes [are] on the ways of {{gender:a person|a man}}, \q and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} sees all {{gender:their|his}} steps.

R.21: God watches how everyone lives. \q He sees every step they take.

decisions.choice: his eyes on the ways: God sees everything people do
decisions.reason: Proverbs 5:21 says the same. Job himself said, "Does he not see my ways and count all my steps?" (31:4); Elihu draws the opposite conclusion from it: God sees, so he judges justly.

decisions.choice: a man: any person
decisions.reason: The word (ish) here means anyone, men and women alike.

decisions.choice: everyone
decisions.reason: Balanced says "everyone", already inclusive; Literal keeps the singular with a gender setting.

records.source: אֵֽין־חֹ֭שֶׁךְוְאֵ֣ין צַלְמָ֑וֶת לְהִסָּ֥תֶר שָׁ֝֗ם פֹּ֣עֲלֵי אָֽוֶן׃
records.gloss: There is no darkness and there is no deep darkness to hide themselves there [the] doers of evil.
pieces: There is no darkness, no deep shadow, \q where evildoers can hide.

L.22: There is no darkness and no deep darkness \q where doers of evil may hide themselves.

R.22: No darkness is deep enough \q for evildoers to hide in.

decisions.choice: deep darkness: thick, deathly darkness
decisions.reason: The word (tsalmavet) is the deepest darkness (3:5; 10:21); it was traditionally read as "shadow of death".

decisions.choice: no darkness can hide from God
decisions.reason: Psalm 139:11-12 says the same. Job had said the wicked use the dark to do their deeds (24:13-17); Elihu answers that God sees them there.

decisions.choice: No darkness is deep enough
alternatives: There is no darkness and no deep darkness
decisions.reason: Readable folds the two words for darkness into one plain phrase.

records.source: כִּ֤י לֹ֣א עַל־אִ֭ישׁ יָשִׂ֣ים ע֑וֹד לַהֲלֹ֥ךְ אֶל־אֵ֝֗ל בַּמִּשְׁפָּֽט׃
records.gloss: For not on a man he sets further to go to God in judgment.
pieces: For {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} does not need to set a time for anyone \q to come before God for judgment.

L.23: For {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} does not set [a time] further for {{gender:a person|a man}} \q to go before God in judgment.

R.23: God does not need to set a day \q for people to come before {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to be judged.

decisions.choice: set further: appoint a time
alternatives: set his mind any longer on a person
decisions.reason: The words are "he does not set further". Many read "he does not set an appointed time" (a small change of one word, to mo'ed), which fits verse 24's "without investigation". Others read "he need not consider a person any further". Either way God needs no hearing to find the truth.

decisions.choice: go to God in judgment: Job's demand for a hearing
decisions.reason: Job has asked again and again for a day in court with God (13:3, 18; 23:3-7). Elihu answers that God does not need such a hearing, because he already sees all (verse 21).

decisions.choice: anyone / people
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use inclusive words; Literal keeps the singular with a gender setting.

records.source: יָרֹ֣עַ כַּבִּירִ֣ים לֹא־חֵ֑קֶר וַיַּעֲמֵ֖ד אֲחֵרִ֣ים תַּחְתָּֽם׃
records.gloss: He breaks mighty ones [with] no searching and sets others in their place.
pieces: He shatters the mighty without any inquiry \q and sets others in their place.

L.24: He shatters mighty ones without investigation \q and sets others in their place.

R.24: He breaks powerful people without needing to look into their case, \q and he puts others in their place.

decisions.choice: no searching: without an inquiry
decisions.reason: The phrase (lo cheqer) elsewhere means "beyond searching out", that is, countless (5:9; 9:10). Here, after verse 23, it most likely means God needs no investigation before he acts, since he already knows what they did (verse 25).

decisions.choice: breaks the mighty and sets others in place
decisions.reason: God brings down rulers and raises up others (Daniel 2:21; Psalm 75:8). Job said much the same of God's power, but as a complaint (12:17-24).

records.source: לָכֵ֗ן יַ֭כִּיר מַעְבָּֽדֵיהֶ֑ם וְהָ֥פַךְ לַ֝֗יְלָה וְיִדַּכָּֽאוּ׃
records.gloss: Therefore he knows their deeds, and he overturns [them in the] night, and they are crushed.
pieces: Because {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} knows what they do, \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} overthrows them in the night, and they are crushed.

L.25: Therefore {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} knows their deeds; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} overturns [them in the] night, and they are crushed.

R.25: Since {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} knows what they do, \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} overthrows them in a single night, and they are crushed.

decisions.choice: therefore: since, for this reason
decisions.reason: The word (lakhen) here gives the ground of verse 24: God can act without inquiry because he already knows what the mighty have done.

decisions.choice: overturns in the night: brings down suddenly
decisions.reason: "Night" recalls the sudden midnight end of verse 20. The verb (hafakh) is used of the overthrow of Sodom (Genesis 19:25).

decisions.choice: Because / Since
decisions.reason: In English "therefore" would make the knowing a result; Balanced and Readable show it as the reason (m1).

records.source: תַּֽחַת־רְשָׁעִ֥ים סְפָקָ֗ם בִּמְק֥וֹם רֹאִֽים׃
records.gloss: In place of wicked ones he strikes them in a place of seers,
pieces: He strikes them down for their wickedness \q where everyone can see,

L.26: As wicked ones {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} strikes them \q in a place where [others] see,

R.26: He punishes them for their evil \q in public, where everyone can see.

decisions.choice: in place of wicked ones: as wicked people, for their wickedness
decisions.reason: The phrase (tachat resha'im) means "in the place of" or "as": God strikes them as the wicked people they are, or for their wickedness.

decisions.choice: strikes them: slaps them, strikes them down
decisions.reason: The verb (safaq) means to slap or clap; here it is God's blow that humiliates.

decisions.choice: in a place of seers: in public
decisions.reason: The punishment is done where others look on, as a public lesson.

decisions.choice: where [others] see
decisions.reason: Literal supplies the subject; "seers" in English would suggest prophets.

records.source: אֲשֶׁ֣ר עַל־כֵּ֭ן סָ֣רוּ מֵֽאַחֲרָ֑יו וְכָל־דְּ֝רָכָ֗יו לֹ֣א הִשְׂכִּֽילוּ׃
records.gloss: because therefore they turned aside from after him, and all his ways not they considered,
pieces: because they turned away from following {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} \q and paid no attention to any of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} ways,

L.27: because they turned aside from following {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} \q and had no regard for any of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} ways,

R.27: This is because they turned away from following {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} \q and ignored all {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} ways.

decisions.choice: because therefore: for the very reason that
decisions.reason: Two words of cause stand together (asher al ken), stressing that this is exactly why they were struck.

decisions.choice: turned aside from after him: stopped following God
decisions.reason: To go after someone is to follow and serve them (1 Kings 18:21); to turn aside from after God is to abandon him.

decisions.choice: considered: paid heed to, understood
decisions.reason: The verb (hiskil) means to give thought to and so act wisely.

decisions.choice: This is because
decisions.reason: Readable starts a new sentence for clarity.

records.source: לְהָבִ֣יא עָ֭לָיו צַֽעֲקַת־דָּ֑ל וְצַעֲקַ֖ת עֲנִיִּ֣ים יִשְׁמָֽע׃
records.gloss: to cause to come to him [the] cry of [the] poor, and [the] cry of [the] afflicted he heard.
pieces: so that they made the cry of the poor reach {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, \q and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} heard the cry of the afflicted.

L.28: so as to bring to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} the cry of the poor; \q and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} heard the cry of the afflicted.

R.28: They made poor people cry out to God, \q and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} heard the cry of those who suffer.

decisions.choice: to cause to come: the result of their wickedness
decisions.reason: The wicked oppressed the poor until their cry reached God. Their wrongdoing brought its own judgment.

decisions.choice: God hears the cry of the poor
decisions.reason: God hears the outcry of the oppressed (Exodus 3:7; 22:22-23; Psalm 34:16). Elihu answers Job's complaint that God ignores the cry of the wounded (24:12).

decisions.choice: God
decisions.reason: Readable names God.

records.source: וְה֤וּא יַשְׁקִ֨ט׀וּמִ֥י יַרְשִׁ֗עַ וְיַסְתֵּ֣ר פָּ֭נִים וּמִ֣י יְשׁוּרֶ֑נּוּ וְעַל־גּ֖וֹי וְעַל־אָדָ֣ם יָֽחַד׃
records.gloss: And he keeps quiet, and who can condemn? And he hides [the] face, and who can see him? And over a nation and over a man alike,
pieces: If {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} stays silent, who can condemn {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}? \q If {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} hides {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} face, who can see {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}? \q Yet {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} rules over nation and individual alike,

L.29: When {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is quiet, who can condemn [{{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}]? \q When {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} hides [{{deity_pronoun:his|His}}] face, who can see {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}? \q [He is] over nation and over {{gender:a person|a man}} alike,

R.29: If God chooses to be silent, who can blame {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}? \q If {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} hides {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} face, who can see {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}? \q Yet {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} rules over nations and over each person,

decisions.choice: condemn: declare guilty
decisions.reason: The verb (yarshia) usually means to declare guilty (verse 17). Some take it here as "who can disturb him?", but the court sense fits the chapter.

decisions.choice: hide the face: withdraw favor and presence
decisions.reason: When God hides his face, he seems absent and does not help (Psalm 13:2; 30:8). Job complained of this (13:24). Elihu answers that God's silence is not injustice.

decisions.choice: over nation and over a man alike: God's rule over all
decisions.reason: The last line goes with verse 30: God rules over nations and single persons alike, so that the godless do not rule.

decisions.choice: rules over
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has no verb in the last line; Balanced and Readable supply "rules", which verse 30 implies.

records.source: מִ֭מְּלֹךְ אָדָ֥ם חָנֵ֗ף מִמֹּ֥קְשֵׁי עָֽם׃
records.gloss: from reigning a man godless, from snares of a people.
pieces: so that the godless may not rule \q and lay snares for the people.

L.30: that a godless {{gender:person|man}} should not reign, \q [nor] be snares for a people.

R.30: so that godless people will not rule \q and trap the people.

decisions.choice: from ... from: so that ... not
decisions.reason: The two "from" phrases are short and hard; the most likely sense is that God's rule prevents a godless ruler from reigning and from trapping the people. The line is difficult and may be damaged.

decisions.choice: godless: profane, without regard for God
decisions.reason: The word (chanef) means godless or profane (8:13; 13:16).

decisions.choice: {{gender:person|man}}
decisions.reason: The word (adam) means a human being; the gender setting gives the traditional form.

records.source: כִּֽי־אֶל־אֵ֭ל הֶאָמַ֥ר נָשָׂ֗אתִי לֹ֣א אֶחְבֹּֽל׃
records.gloss: For to God has [anyone] said, I have borne, not I will act corruptly;
pieces: Suppose someone says to God, "I have borne my punishment; \q I will not do wrong again.

L.31: For has [anyone] said to God, "I have borne [punishment]; \q I will not act corruptly [again].

R.31: Suppose someone said to God, \q "I have been punished, and I will not sin anymore.

decisions.choice: has anyone said: a supposed case
decisions.reason: The question form sets up a case: suppose a person says this to God. The words of the penitent run on into verse 32, and verse 33 asks whether God must then repay on Job's terms. Verses 31-33 are among the hardest in the book.

decisions.choice: I have borne: I have borne my punishment
decisions.reason: The verb (nasa) is "bear" or "carry"; with no object it most likely means "I have borne my punishment".

decisions.choice: act corruptly: do wrong, offend
decisions.reason: The verb (chaval) means to act corruptly or do harm (Nehemiah 1:7).

decisions.choice: Suppose someone says
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable turn the question into the supposed case it introduces (m1).

records.source: בִּלְעֲדֵ֣י אֶ֭חֱזֶה אַתָּ֣ה הֹרֵ֑נִי אִֽם־עָ֥וֶל פָּ֝עַ֗לְתִּי לֹ֣א אֹסִֽיף׃
records.gloss: Apart from [what] I see, you teach me; if wrong I have done, not I will do [it] again.
pieces: Teach me what I cannot see; \q if I have done wrong, I will do it no more."

L.32: What I do not see, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} teach me; \q if I have done wrong, I will not do [it] again"?

R.32: Show me the wrong I cannot see. \q If I have done wrong, I will not do it again."

decisions.choice: apart from what I see, you teach me: a prayer for insight
decisions.reason: The penitent asks God to show him faults he cannot see for himself (Psalm 19:13). Elihu hints that this is what Job should say.

decisions.choice: wrong: injustice
decisions.reason: The word (avel) is wrong or injustice, the same word Elihu denied of God in verse 10.

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} teach me
decisions.reason: The speaker addresses God, so "you" takes the deity pronoun setting.

decisions.choice: Teach me / Show me
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make it the request it is.

records.source: הַֽמֵעִמְּךָ֬ יְשַׁלְמֶ֨נָּה כִּֽי־מָאַ֗סְתָּ כִּי־אַתָּ֣ה תִבְחַ֣ר וְלֹא־אָ֑נִי וּֽמַה־יָדַ֥עְתָּ דַבֵּֽר׃
records.gloss: From with you will he repay it, because you have rejected? For you must choose, and not I; and what you know, speak.
pieces: Should {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} repay on your terms when you have rejected {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} way? \q You must choose, not I; \q so tell us what you know.

L.33: Should {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} repay it on your terms, since you have rejected [it]? \q For you must choose, and not I; \q so speak what you know.

R.33: Should God pay you back the way you want, \q when you refuse what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} does? \q You must decide, not I. So tell us what you know.

decisions.choice: from with you: on your terms
decisions.reason: The words are "from with you will he repay it?". The most likely sense is "should God repay as you think fit?", addressed to Job. The verse is very hard, and its object ("it") and what Job "rejected" are not stated.

decisions.choice: you have rejected ... you must choose, and not I
decisions.reason: Job has rejected God's way of dealing with him, so it is Job who must decide what to say, not Elihu. Elihu presses him to speak if he knows better.

decisions.choice: rejected {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} way
decisions.reason: The Hebrew gives no object; Balanced supplies the one the context implies (God's way of dealing with Job).

decisions.choice: God
decisions.reason: Readable names God.

records.source: אַנְשֵׁ֣י לֵ֭בָב יֹ֣אמְרוּ לִ֑י וְגֶ֥בֶר חָ֝כָ֗ם שֹׁמֵ֥עַֽ לִֽי׃
records.gloss: Men of heart will say to me, and a man wise who hears me:
pieces: {{gender:People|Men}} of understanding will say to me, \q and so will any wise {{gender:person|man}} who hears me:

L.34: {{gender:People|Men}} of heart will say to me, \q and {{gender:a wise person|a wise man}} who hears me:

R.34: People who understand will tell me, \q and so will any wise person listening to me:

decisions.choice: men of heart: people of understanding
decisions.reason: As in verse 10, the heart is the seat of understanding.

decisions.choice: will say: the verdict follows in verses 35-37
decisions.reason: Elihu claims that any sensible listener will agree with his verdict on Job.

decisions.choice: people / person
decisions.reason: The words (anshe, gever) here mean any wise listener; the inclusive forms are the default, with the traditional ones as the setting's alternative (Readable needs no span).

records.source: אִ֭יּוֹב לֹא־בְדַ֣עַת יְדַבֵּ֑ר וּ֝דְבָרָ֗יו לֹ֣א בְהַשְׂכֵּֽיל׃
records.gloss: Job not with knowledge speaks, and his words [are] not with insight.
pieces: Job speaks without knowledge; \q his words show no insight.

L.35: Job speaks without knowledge, \q and his words [are] without insight.

R.35: Job does not know what he is talking about. \q His words make no sense.

decisions.choice: speaks without knowledge
decisions.reason: The LORD will use similar words, "words without knowledge" (38:2), and Job will admit that he spoke of things he did not understand (42:3).

decisions.choice: insight: understanding that leads to wise speech
decisions.reason: The word (haskel) is the insight of the wise (Proverbs 21:11).

decisions.choice: does not know what he is talking about
decisions.reason: Readable uses an everyday phrase for the same judgment.

records.source: אָבִ֗י יִבָּחֵ֣ן אִיּ֣וֹב עַד־נֶ֑צַח עַל־תְּ֝שֻׁבֹ֗ת בְּאַנְשֵׁי־אָֽוֶן׃
records.gloss: Would that Job were tested to [the] end, for answers among men of wickedness.
pieces: If only Job were tested to the limit \q for answering like the wicked!

L.36: Would that Job were tested to the end \q for [his] answers like {{gender:people|men}} of evil!

R.36: I wish Job would be tested all the way, \q because he answers like evil people do.

decisions.choice: would that: a wish
decisions.reason: The word (avi) is most likely a word of wishing, "oh that". It looks like "my father", and some take it as Elihu calling on God as Father, but that would be unusual in the Old Testament.

decisions.choice: tested to the end: tried thoroughly
decisions.reason: The verb (bachan) is to test, as metal is tested; "to the end" (ad netsach) means completely. Elihu wants Job's trial carried through until his words are judged.

decisions.choice: answers among men of wickedness: answering as the wicked do
decisions.reason: The preposition (be) here means "like" or "in the manner of": Job's answers sound like those of the wicked (verse 8).

records.source: כִּ֥י יֹ֘סִ֤יף עַֽל־חַטָּאת֣וֹ פֶ֭שַׁע בֵּינֵ֣ינוּ יִסְפּ֑וֹק וְיֶ֖רֶב אֲמָרָ֣יו לָאֵֽל׃ס
records.gloss: For he adds to his sin rebellion; among us he claps, and multiplies his words to God.
pieces: For he adds rebellion to his sin; he claps his hands at us in scorn \q and piles up his words against God.

L.37: For he adds rebellion to his sin; among us he claps [his hands], \q and he multiplies his words against God.

R.37: He is adding rebellion to his sin and mocks us by clapping his hands. \q He keeps piling up words against God.

decisions.choice: sin, rebellion: wrong made worse by defiance
decisions.reason: Sin (chatta't) is missing the mark; rebellion (pesha) is defiance against God. Elihu says Job's words have turned whatever sin he had into open revolt.

decisions.choice: claps: a gesture of scorn
decisions.reason: Clapping the hands at someone is a sign of contempt (27:23; Lamentations 2:15).

decisions.choice: to God: against God
decisions.reason: The preposition (le) with "multiply words" means words aimed at God, against him.

decisions.choice: claps his hands ... in scorn / mocks us by clapping his hands
decisions.reason: English needs the hands, and the meaning of the gesture (m2).
